paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this passage. The builders get stopped cold by the governor himself, with his whole crew and a clipboard full of questions, and they keep building anyway. Why? Because "the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, so that they were not stopped" (Ezra 5:5). Their work didn't stand on their own nerve. It stood on His eye being on them.

Now look at how the elders answer when somebody asks who gave them the right. They don't puff up. They say, "We are servants of the God of heaven and earth" (Ezra 5:11). They also tell the hard part out loud, that their fathers angered God (Ezra 5:12), and then they point to the good part, a decree from Cyrus (Ezra 5:13). That's an honest answer, baker. No hiding, no spin, just who they serve and what they were told to do.

So what do you take home? When your work for God gets questioned, you don't have to panic, and you don't have to have every answer polished. Know whose servant you are, tell the truth, and keep your hands on the work while the answer is still on its way. I spent years waiting in the dark on somebody else's decision, so I'm telling you, His eye finds the ones who wait. And this story is NOT done.
